title: OMNEX Engine — cost, latency, errors
description: Panels are ordered by the question they answer: is it up, is it fast, is it correct, what does it cost. Every percentile panel queries the histogram buckets via histogram_quantile — never a pre-averaged percentile, which is arithmetically meaningless across instances.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Failed runs over all runs. Paged above 5% sustained for 3 minutes.

panels.title: Cost per request
panels.description: Unit economics, independent of traffic. This is what catches a bad prompt change: total spend rises with traffic and looks normal while this quietly triples.

panels.title: Burn rate
panels.description: USD/hour from a pico-dollar counter. A rate alert fires while there is still something to do about it; a monthly-total alert fires once the money is gone.

panels.title: Prompt cache hit ratio
panels.description: Cached input tokens over all input tokens. A collapsed cache is invisible in latency and error panels — only the bill notices.

panels.title: Run latency percentiles
panels.description: Computed with histogram_quantile over summed bucket rates. Never average per-instance percentiles: two instances each reporting p95=100ms do not imply a fleet p95 of 100ms, and no arithmetic on those two numbers recovers the real one.

panels.title: p95 by step
panels.description: Which stage owns the tail. Retrieval, rerank and generation fail differently and a single run-level percentile hides which one moved.

panels.title: Spend by model
panels.description: Stacked USD/hour per model. The router's escalation rate shows up here first: a cheap tier that stops carrying traffic is a routing regression, not a traffic change.

panels.title: Tokens by direction
panels.description: Input, output and cached-input. Cached input is a subset of input, not an addition — see core/money.py.

panels.title: Errors by code
panels.description: Grouped by the stable machine-readable code, not by message text, so a reworded error does not split into a new series.

panels.title: Cardinality overflow
panels.description: Non-zero means a label hit its cap and observations are folding into __overflow__. Totals stay correct; every breakdown by that label does not. Published rather than logged, because a metric that silently stopped being a breakdown is one people keep reading.
